title: Les adjectifs possessifs
ruleNote: Possessive adjectives say who owns something: my, your, his, her, our, their. In French the form changes with the noun owned, not the owner. This module walks through mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes, son/sa/ses, notre/nos, votre/vos and leur/leurs, plus the vowel trick (mon amie).

elements.label: L'adjectif possessif s'accorde au nom
elements.ruleNote: A possessive matches the thing owned, not the owner: it is the gender and number of the noun that decides the form.

examples.explanation: Chien is masculine, so the form is mon.
Voiture is feminine, so the form is ma.
Livres is plural, so the form is mes.
Maison is feminine singular, so ma.
Café is masculine singular, so mon.

elements.label: mon (masculin)
elements.ruleNote: Use 'mon' for 'my' before a masculine singular noun: mon chien, mon livre. The owner is 'I', but mon matches the noun.

examples.explanation: Garçon is masculine singular, so mon.
Pain is masculine singular, so mon.

elements.label: ma (féminin)
elements.ruleNote: Use 'ma' before a feminine singular noun: ma voiture, ma maison. Same owner 'I', feminine noun gives ma.

examples.explanation: Table is feminine singular, so ma.
Fille is feminine singular, so ma.

elements.label: mes (pluriel)
elements.ruleNote: Use 'mes' for 'my' before any plural noun: mes chiens, mes amies. One form covers both genders in the plural.

examples.explanation: Pommes is plural, so mes (even though pomme is feminine).
examples.hint: Plural means mes for any gender.

elements.label: mon devant une voyelle
elements.ruleNote: Before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, use 'mon', not ma: mon amie, mon école. It keeps the smooth sound.

examples.explanation: Amie is feminine but starts with a vowel, so mon.
examples.hint: Vowel start, so mon even though amie is feminine.

examples.explanation: École is feminine but vowel-initial, so mon.
Eau is feminine but vowel-initial, so mon.
Amie is vowel-initial, so mon, not ma.
examples.hint: Vowel start beats the feminine rule.

elements.label: ton / ta / tes
elements.ruleNote: 'your' (informal, one owner): ton chien, ta voiture, tes amis. Same gender/number logic as mon/ma/mes.

examples.explanation: Maison is feminine singular, so ta.

elements.label: ton devant une voyelle
elements.ruleNote: Like mon, use 'ton' before a vowel even for a feminine noun: ton amie, ton école. Avoids 'ta amie'.

examples.explanation: Amie is vowel-initial, so ton, not ta.

examples.hint: Vowel start beats the feminine rule.

elements.label: son / sa / ses
elements.ruleNote: 'his/her/its': son chien, sa voiture, ses livres. French does not show the owner's gender, only the noun's.

examples.explanation: Maison is feminine singular, so sa.

elements.label: son = his ou her
elements.ruleNote: 'son livre' can mean 'his book' or 'her book' — the form depends on 'livre' (masculine), not on who owns it. Context tells you which.

examples.explanation: Livre is masculine, so son even though the owner is female.
examples.hint: The form follows livre, not Marie.

examples.prompt: Construis : « Paul looks at his car. »
examples.explanation: Voiture is feminine, so sa even though the owner is male.
examples.hint: The form follows voiture, not Paul.

examples.prompt: Choisis : Marie aime ___ chat. (Marie loves her cat)
examples.explanation: Chat is masculine, so son, whoever owns it.

examples.prompt: Choisis : Paul cherche ___ maison. (Paul looks for his house)
examples.explanation: Maison is feminine, so sa, whoever owns it.

elements.label: son devant une voyelle
elements.ruleNote: Use 'son' before a vowel even for a feminine noun: son amie, son école. Same vowel rule as mon and ton.

examples.explanation: Amie is vowel-initial, so son, not sa.

examples.hint: Vowel start beats the feminine rule.

elements.label: notre (singulier)
elements.ruleNote: 'our' before a singular noun is 'notre' for both genders: notre maison, notre chien. No separate masculine/feminine form.

examples.hint: Notre works for masculine and feminine.

examples.explanation: Voiture is singular, so notre (same as masculine).
examples.hint: Notre fits any gender in the singular.

elements.label: nos (pluriel)
elements.ruleNote: 'our' before a plural noun is 'nos': nos amis, nos voitures. notre/nos is just singular vs plural.

elements.label: votre (singulier)
elements.ruleNote: 'your' (formal/plural) before a singular noun is 'votre': votre livre, votre maison. Same form for both genders.

elements.label: vos (pluriel)
elements.ruleNote: 'your' before a plural noun is 'vos': vos enfants, vos amis. votre/vos mirrors notre/nos.

elements.label: leur (singulier)
elements.ruleNote: 'their' before a singular noun is 'leur': leur maison, leur chien. One form for both genders.

examples.hint: Leur works for any gender in the singular.

elements.label: leurs (pluriel)
elements.ruleNote: 'their' before a plural noun is 'leurs', with an -s: leurs amis, leurs voitures. The -s marks the plural of the noun, not the owners.

elements.label: leur vs leurs
elements.ruleNote: Choose by the noun: one thing gives leur (leur chien), several things give leurs (leurs chiens). The number of owners never matters.

elements.label: Possessif vs article
elements.ruleNote: A possessive replaces the article: say 'mon chien', never 'le mon chien'. You use one or the other, not both.

examples.explanation: The possessive mon replaces the article, so no le.
examples.hint: Drop the article; mon already does its job.

examples.explanation: Ma replaces la, so no article.
Use ma alone, never with an article.
examples.hint: Possessive instead of article, not both.

examples.explanation: Use son alone, never with le.

elements.label: Choisir le bon possessif
elements.ruleNote: Two questions: who owns it (my/your/his...) and what is the noun (masc/fem/plural)? Both answers pick the exact form.

elements.label: Synthèse : les adjectifs possessifs
elements.ruleNote: Put it together: identify the owner, then match the noun's gender and number, and use mon/ton/son before a vowel.
